lesson_title: The Yard That Needs a Magnet Crane
hook_text: A bakkie tips a pile of mixed metal. Copper is worth a fortune, steel is worth a little, and mixed is worth nothing.
clip_script: A scrap dealer in Germiston gets a jumble of metal every day. The mill will not buy it mixed. Workers sort by hand and cut their fingers. So what is the need? Not a crane. The need is to separate the metal a magnet grabs from the metal it ignores, fast and safely. A crane with a magnet is one answer. Now look at real cranes. Every one has a base, a body, an arm, a cable over a pulley, and a hook or magnet. They hoist, they luff, they slew. And they do not fall over, because of a counterweight or wide legs. Borrow those ideas, sketch them small, and remember the magnet must switch off to let go. That means an electromagnet. Your model will lift paper clips, not tonnes, but the idea is the same.
visual_style: Whiteboard pile of scrap splitting into two heaps; simple crane outline with parts labelled one by one; a counterweight sliding on to stop the tip.
mood: Curious and practical, a real problem with a visible answer.
pacing: Fast scenario, pause on the need, quick tour of crane parts, close on the switch-off magnet.
